desk.headline: Revenue down 1% to RMB30.8bn, slightly above estimates; AI cloud up 94% but ad slump squeezes profit; no guidance

other.label: Net income to Baidu
other.change: vs loss of RMB11.2bn a year ago

results: Total revenue slipped 1% to RMB30.8bn, just above the RMB30.6bn estimate; iQIYI fell 10% to RMB6.0bn.
The core Baidu business returned to growth, up 1%, as AI cloud revenue nearly doubled to RMB8.2bn (GPU cloud +191%).
Online marketing kept shrinking, down 22% to RMB11.9bn, and now makes up under half of core revenue.
Adjusted EPS fell 39% to RMB6.78 per ADS but beat the RMB6.16 estimate; GAAP net income was RMB1.4bn after a large impairment loss a year ago.
Operating cash flow was RMB2.8bn, but heavy capital spending (RMB7.3bn) left free cash flow at -RMB4.6bn; cash and investments stood at RMB276.6bn.

guidance.summary: Baidu does not give numeric guidance. It repeated that it expects to declare its first dividend before the end of 2026, subject to board approval.

points: AI cloud demand stays strong: the three biggest GPU cloud customers renewed on multi-year contracts and more customers are paying upfront.
Advertising is expected to stay under pressure from the economy, competition and the shift to AI search, where user experience comes before near-term revenue.
Q3 capital spending was about RMB4bn lower than Q2; new spending will be paced to customer demand and cash collection.
The Kunlunxin M100 chip is close to volume production, with the M300 planned for next year.
Management expects profit to stay under pressure near term; buybacks of about $373m so far this year will continue.
call.source: Q3 2026 earnings call transcript — Investing.com, 16 Nov 2026

watch: Whether AI cloud growth keeps outpacing the decline in online advertising.
Size and timing of the first dividend promised before year-end.
Capital spending and free cash flow as AI investment continues.
